title: Pivot-exchange Gray codes for spanning trees
formal: Does every finite connected simple undirected graph have a pivot-exchange listing of all its spanning trees?
definitions: Let G=(V,E) have at least one vertex, no loops and no parallel edges. A spanning tree is an edge subset connecting all vertices without a cycle; the one-vertex tree is the empty set. A listing T_1,…,T_m contains every spanning tree exactly once. For every 1≤i<m require T_(i+1)=(T_i\{e_i})∪{f_i}, with e_i∈T_i, f_i∈E\T_i, and the edges e_i,f_i sharing at least one endpoint. No adjacency is required between T_m and T_1. Neither an efficient algorithm nor a prescribed first tree is part of the proposition.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of this existence proposition or a counterexample with a proof that no such listing exists.
context: The source proves the property for outerplanar graphs and states the general graph question separately. The directed arborescence question would imply this one.
why: A pivot-exchange ordering would impose a much stronger locality condition than ordinary edge-exchange enumeration.
